solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, enumeration length); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's answer wrong at 12 across, corrected here

entries.clue: Engineer at Brunel being revolutionary? (8)

indicatorNotes.Engineer: to engineer something is to rework and rebuild it, so the letters are rebuilt

annotation.surface: A question about whether the great Victorian engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel was a radical.
annotation.walkthrough: Brunel's fame as an engineer makes 'Engineer' read as a job title; here it is the instruction. 'Revolutionary' is taken literally: able to revolve, with the question mark flagging the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Something turnable can be turned round, so it is revolutionary in the sense of able to revolve.

entries.clue: I finally got IT nerd hyped and pent up about work (3,5,7)

indicatorNotes.hyped: hyped up means overexcited and jumbled, so the letters are stirred
indicatorNotes.up: stirred up, so the letters are mixed
indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the mixed letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: op = opus, a work, placed inside the mixed letters

annotation.surface: A tech worker, wound up and frustrated about their job, at last understands something.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitalised IT looks like information technology beside 'nerd', but it is just 'it' in 'I finally got it'. The mixed letters go round OP.
annotation.definitionFit: When the penny drops, you finally understand something, so 'the penny dropped' says 'I finally got it'.

entries.clue: Restabilise prices agent initially exaggerated grossly (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

annotation.surface: A report that an agent's exaggeration was grossly out of line with efforts to steady prices.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initially' governs both following words, taking E and G. To repeg a currency is to fix its value again against another.
annotation.definitionFit: To repeg is to fix a price or currency rate again, making it stable once more.

entries.clue: A Sartre novel featuring old penetrating sorts? (8)

indicatorNotes.novel: novel means new, so the letters take a new order
indicatorNotes.featuring: featuring means including, so the mixed letters include O

blocks.note: o = old, as in dictionary abbreviations

annotation.surface: A novel by Jean-Paul Sartre with elderly characters who probe deeply.
annotation.walkthrough: Sartre makes 'novel' read as a book; it is the anagram signal. Aerators are tools that spike holes in lawns, hence the question mark on 'penetrating sorts'.
annotation.definitionFit: Aerators push spikes or tines into soil to let air in, so they are things that penetrate.

entries.clue: Meal for one? (5)

blocks.note: the definition: a meal, read plainly
the surface suggests a single diner; 'one' is really the time of day, one o'clock

annotation.walkthrough: 'For one' reads as a meal for a single person; the 'one' is the hour, one o'clock, when lunch is eaten.
annotation.definitionFit: Lunch is the midday meal, typically eaten around one o'clock.

entries.clue: Boat behind base (6)

blocks.note: nautical: a ship, or its hull below the waterline
your rear, the part you sit on

annotation.surface: A boat moored behind a naval base.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: all three words mean BOTTOM. The nautical sense, a ship or its hull, is the one solvers are least likely to know.
annotation.definitionFit: Bottom means a ship, the seat you sit on, and the lowest part of anything.

entries.clue: Ill-mannered pensioner cut short by Sturgeon? (6)

indicatorNotes.cut short: cut short means the last letter is chopped off

blocks.note: OAP (old-age pensioner) minus its last letter
a sturgeon is an example of a fish, as the question mark signals

annotation.surface: A rude old-age pensioner is cut off mid-sentence by Nicola Sturgeon, the former Scottish First Minister.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital S makes Sturgeon the politician; here she is just a kind of fish. OAP is the British abbreviation for old-age pensioner.
annotation.definitionFit: Oafish means clumsy and boorish, like an oaf, which is ill-mannered.

entries.clue: Lady with an Edwardian dresser (5,4)

blocks.note: a young woman, not a titled one
a 'dresser' here is a person who dresses: a 1950s youth in Edwardian-style clothes

annotation.walkthrough: 'Dresser' reads as a valet or a piece of furniture; it is a man who dresses Edwardian. Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits, and teddy girls went with them.
annotation.definitionFit: A teddy girl was the girlfriend of a teddy boy, a young man who dressed in Edwardian fashion.

entries.clue: Business giant merged disastrously with Rank (6,9)

indicatorNotes.disastrously: a disaster wrecks things, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, joined to the rest by 'with'

annotation.surface: A corporate giant's merger with the Rank Organisation, a British film and leisure company, went badly.
annotation.walkthrough: Rank's capital makes it the company; the word is only letters. Market gardening is growing vegetables and fruit commercially for sale.
annotation.definitionFit: Market gardening is a trade, growing produce to sell, so it is a business.

entries.clue: Choose to hide old literature or prosecute MP’s activity? (8)

indicatorNotes.to hide: to hide something is to keep it inside, so PICK holds the other letters

annotation.surface: A choice between concealing old writings and taking a member of parliament to court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prosecute' here means carry on, not take to court: to politick is to carry on an MP's business of politics.
annotation.definitionFit: To politick is to engage in political activity, which is carrying on what an MP does.

entries.clue: Reason pet needs treatment for tongue (9)

indicatorNotes.needs treatment: treatment works on something and changes it, so the letters change order

annotation.surface: A vet explains why a pet must be treated for something wrong with its tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: The vet's-surgery picture makes 'tongue' a body part; it means a language.
annotation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international language, and a tongue is a language.

entries.clue: Plug in iron close to Pioneer audio device (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in means placed inside, so AD goes inside FE
indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its end, so take the last letter

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a plug is a piece of advertising, an ad

annotation.surface: Instructions for plugging an iron into a Pioneer, a brand of hi-fi equipment.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'plug' electrical; it means a promotional mention.
annotation.definitionFit: A fader is a sliding control on a mixing desk that raises or lowers a sound signal.

blocks.note: not arithmetic: take the letters of 17 across out of 29 across, leaving a word for a boat's rowers
that leftover word is a synonym of this answer, from rowing

annotation.walkthrough: The numbers are clue references, not sums. SCREWING minus SING leaves CREW, and a racing crew of eight rowers is called an eight.
annotation.definitionFit: A racing rowing boat with eight oarsmen, and its crew, is called an eight.

entries.clue: You could say Faux Bob’s a slithery criminal (9)

indicatorNotes.criminal: criminal means crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

annotation.surface: Someone warns that a man called Bob, a fake, is a slippery crook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun describing Bob; it is an adjective telling you to mix the letters. A faux bob is a style where long hair is pinned under to look short.
annotation.definitionFit: A faux bob is a way of arranging long hair to mimic a bob, so it is a hairstyle.

entries.clue: Winter ban on booze broken by isle and island (3,7)

indicatorNotes.on booze: someone on booze is drunk and all over the place, so the letters are mixed
indicatorNotes.broken by: broken by means split open with something put in, so I goes inside

annotation.surface: A seasonal prohibition on alcohol is broken on some island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ban on booze' reads as prohibition; 'on booze' is the anagram signal, and 'ban' is fodder. New Britain is the largest island of the Bismarck Archipelago, in Papua New Guinea.
annotation.definitionFit: New Britain is an island in the Bismarck Archipelago, part of Papua New Guinea.

entries.clue: Pale ale for one in drink (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes where the answer lives: a white bass is a fish found in the drink, i.e. the water

blocks.note: Bass is a brand of ale; 'for one' signals an example

annotation.surface: A pale ale being offered as one choice in a round of drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea or water, so something 'in drink' is a fish. The white bass is a North American freshwater fish.
annotation.definitionFit: The white bass is a freshwater fish, so it is found in the drink, meaning water.

entries.clue: Tea break interrupted by one most emotional, perhaps (8)

indicatorNotes.interrupted by: interrupted by means something breaks in, so I goes inside REST

annotation.surface: A tea break is cut in on by whoever is most upset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tea break' reads as one phrase; tea is kept as it stands and break is the rest. 'Perhaps' signals that tears are only one way of being emotional.
annotation.definitionFit: Tearful people are emotional, so the tearest, or most tearful, can be called most emotional.

entries.clue: Confess US evil and head for Guantanamo (4)

indicatorNotes.head for: the head of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: An order to admit America's wickedness and go to Guantanamo, the US prison camp in Cuba.
annotation.walkthrough: 'US' reads as America in the surface, but it tags the definition: to sing is American slang for confessing to the police.
annotation.definitionFit: In American slang, a suspect who sings tells the police everything, which is confessing.

entries.clue: Not any point saving last of Belgian waffle (8)

indicatorNotes.saving: saving means keeping safe inside, so NO SENSE holds the letter
indicatorNotes.last of: last of means the final letter

blocks.note: there is no sense in it = there isn't any point

annotation.surface: There is no use rescuing the last Belgian waffle.
annotation.walkthrough: Next to 'Belgian', 'waffle' is a breakfast; it is the definition, empty talk. 'Saving' means keeping safe inside, not rescuing.
annotation.definitionFit: Waffle is talk that says nothing sensible, which is nonsense.

entries.clue: Murder and execution … that’s no good (2,2)

indicatorNotes.no good: no good means without G, the abbreviation for good

blocks.note: execution of a task is the doing of it

annotation.surface: A remark that murder and capital punishment are both wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: Next to 'murder', 'execution' reads as capital punishment; it means carrying something out, DOING.
annotation.definitionFit: To do someone in is to kill them, so do in means murder.

entries.clue: According to Spooner, foul cricketer’s an angel (10)

indicatorNotes.According to Spooner: Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so swap the opening sounds

blocks.note: rank = foul; its R swaps with the B of the next word
a bowler is a cricketer; its B swaps with the R of the first word

annotation.surface: A claim that a nasty cricket player is, in fact, a heavenly being.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Angel' is theatre slang for someone who puts money into a show. A bowler is the cricketer who delivers the ball.
annotation.definitionFit: An angel is a financial backer, especially of a stage production, which is a bankroller.

entries.clue: Old period property (6)

blocks.note: an archaic sense: a stage or condition of life, as when a boy reaches manhood
land and buildings, especially a large country holding

annotation.surface: A property dating from some historical era, like a period home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old period property' reads as an estate agent's phrase. 'Old' tags the first sense as dated: estate once meant a period or condition of life.
annotation.definitionFit: Estate once meant a stage or period of life, and still means a large property.

entries.clue: Surplus ball on several deliveries of balls (9)

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, so several are overs
a pill is a small ball; it goes on (after) OVERS

annotation.surface: A cricket scene: an extra ball bowled on top of several overs.
annotation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler.
annotation.definitionFit: Overspill is what spills over, an excess, so it is surplus.

entries.clue: Line of oily rickshaws (5)

indicatorNotes.of: of means taken from, so the answer sits inside the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap, after 'oi' and before 'kshaws'

annotation.surface: A row of greasy rickshaws.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Line of' reads as a queue; 'Line' is the definition and 'of' points into the words. A lyric is the words of a song, and a single line can be called one.
annotation.definitionFit: A lyric is the words of a song, so a sung line counts as one.

entries.clue: Runner showing sound judgement in hearing (5)

indicatorNotes.in hearing: in hearing means as heard, so take the sound

annotation.surface: An athlete shows good sense at a court hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is a crossword word for a river, which runs. The Seine flows through Paris.
annotation.definitionFit: The Seine is a river, and a river runs, so it is a runner.

entries.clue: Old people can be cool … flipping cool (5)

indicatorNotes.flipping: flipping means turning over, so the word runs backwards

annotation.surface: An exasperated remark that the elderly can be cool, really cool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word; it is the reversal signal. The Iceni were the ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.
annotation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a Celtic tribe of ancient Britain, so they are an old people.

entries.clue: A nuke about to engulf large open space (5)

indicatorNotes.about: about means turned round, so A ZAP runs backwards
indicatorNotes.to engulf: to engulf is to swallow, so the reversed letters hold L

blocks.note: to nuke something is to zap it
L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A nuclear strike is about to wipe out a big open area.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'going to'; 'about' is the reversal and 'to engulf' the container. L goes inside PAZA after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plaza is a public square, an open space in a town.

entries.clue: Plain and clear about German backing Congress (9)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so SERENE goes around G

blocks.note: a clear, calm sky is serene
congress is sexual intercourse, and IT is slang for sex

annotation.surface: A plain-spoken verdict about a German supporting the US Congress.
annotation.walkthrough: Capitalised, 'Congress' looks like the US legislature; it means sexual congress, IT. 'Plain' is the definition, not an adjective. The Serengeti is a vast plain in Tanzania.
annotation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a huge grassland plain in Tanzania and Kenya.

entries.clue: Well put-together types of food containers (6)

blocks.note: a dish is an attractive person
plates and bowls that hold food

annotation.surface: A description of well-made kinds of food container.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Well put-together' reads like sturdy workmanship; it describes good-looking people, dishes in slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Attractive people are called dishes, and dishes are also bowls or plates for food.

entries.clue: King admitted to engaging in darn cheating (8)

indicatorNotes.admitted to: admitted to means let inside, so CR goes into SEWING

blocks.note: someone engaged in darning is sewing

annotation.surface: A king is let in on some dishonest scheme, with a mild curse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Darn' reads as a mild oath; it means mending by sewing. CR, for Carolus Rex, is the royal cipher of King Charles.
annotation.definitionFit: To screw someone is slang for cheating them, so screwing means cheating.
